title: Fuse the gate projection and GLU epilogue
reason: Source-only final checkpoint. The kernel is committed and source review is complete with no remaining blocking finding, but nothing was compiled, executed or measured: compilation, runtime, math and performance checks are all not run, no numerical check is claimed to have passed, and shader compilation is not claimed to work. The scope is epilogue-only and independent of 011a: the gate projection W_gate*x -> F32 sigmoid -> MUL with the factor a is fused into the STORE of the ordinary (non-tensor) simdgroup matrix-multiply kernel, eliding the gate-MM and sigmoid intermediates and their two standalone elementwise dispatches while still materializing the final MUL output. The separate factor projection a = Wa*x and its materialization remain, so this is not a two-projection or concatenated-weight kernel. No measured result is transferred from any other trial.

safety_contract: Implemented and source-reviewed; unexecuted. Generic public-output, view and extra-consumer protections are retained: the pattern is a regular elision chain, so the generic chain, subgraph elidable-use and memory-range checks still apply.
All activations (x, factor, gate MM, sigmoid, MUL) must share one Metal buffer, while weights may be separate.
FULL matching rejects final-output overlap with W or x, and MM/sigmoid overlap with the factor.

FULL matching rejects either elided MM/sigmoid output overlapping either W or x: the ordinary sequence has already overwritten those bytes by the time a later consumer runs, while the fused execution would skip the intermediate stores.
Only the exact final-in-place factor is permitted; partial overlap is rejected.
Both Metal-buffer intervals and underlying host addresses are checked, so multiple wrappers over one host arena cannot hide an alias.
The pattern is skipped in the allocation-dependency pass: zero new allocation dependencies and no extended input lifetimes; unsafe aliases are rejected at full matching after allocation.

Implemented same-buffer negatives (final cases commit), one Metal buffer with a trailing add(mul, aliased input) and both MUL operand orders, none of which may fuse: raw_sigmoid_x (sigmoid storage exactly over the activation), raw_sigmoid_x_partial (16 bytes into the activation) and raw_sigmoid_w (over the F32 weight head, read back through a legitimate view of the weight). The runner binds the whole triple, weight included, into a single buffer object at page-aligned slots, so plain tensor identities carry the alias and no view_src is forged.
Mapped-wrapper negatives mapped_out_x / mapped_sigmoid_x / mapped_mm_a bind one host arena through two distinct Metal mappings and must stay unfused.
numerics: Full tiles retain the original K loop, operand staging, accumulators, workgroup geometry and stores; the factor tile is loaded at the same simdgroup tile origin and leading dimension, pairing each thread element with the matching gate accumulator element.
Tail tiles keep the existing scratch and barriers and apply the epilogue only to valid float4/scalar stores; the factor rows of a partial tile stay inside the valid tail.

Sigmoid is the ordinary 1/(1+exp(-gate)) evaluated with an intended F32 intermediate before a separately evaluated product; the multiply uses safe math and contract-off semantics in the fused MUL's original operand order. The full-tile path evaluates the sigmoid per scalar, while the existing standalone unary path operates on float4 values.

Compiler math and rounding therefore require an actual hardware bit comparison of the full-tile scalar sigmoid against the standalone float4 unary result; source equivalence is not evidence of exact bits, and no such comparison has been run.

Staging on this pinned backend: with default source precision, this ordinary large-MM path stages operands in half, including F32-weight × F32-activation storage; an explicit F32 src[1] hint selects F32 operand staging only for the F32-weight × F32-activation kernel. The gate's UNDEFINED src[1] requirement is a conservative eligibility check applied to all four weight types, separate from this staging selection. No precision threshold is relaxed.

arithmetic.caveat: Arithmetic counts only, not measured performance, memory-bandwidth or allocator-peak savings; extra epilogue registers and factor loads may offset the benefit.

Diagnostic counts, not a substitute for ordinary worker timing.
